title: Why Your Brain Hates Rewards for Fun Things
hook: Giving a child money for reading can make them read less.

narration.text: Giving a child money for reading can make them read less.
This is because of something called intrinsic versus extrinsic motivation.
Intrinsic motivation comes from internal enjoyment, doing something for its own sake.
Extrinsic motivation is doing something for an external reward, like money or praise.
When an enjoyable task gets an external reward, our brain reclassifies it.
It switches from a fun activity to a task done for payment.
This can diminish the original internal joy and reduce your drive.
So, be careful how you incentivise things you genuinely love.
Have you noticed this effect in your own hobbies or work?

description: Ever wonder why a reward can sometimes make you less interested in an activity? This short explains the psychological difference between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, and how external rewards can surprisingly diminish your inner drive for things you once loved to do.
topic: Why external rewards can sometimes decrease your inner drive, explaining intrinsic versus extrinsic motivation.
